chase_cards.name: Lucky Stadium [Diglett] [Tōhoku]
chase_cards.why: This is a chase because the Tōhoku print makes the regional Stadium almost quietly strange: Diglett, islands, shrine architecture, and a Sendai tournament route all compress into one local prize card.

key_artists.name: Yuichi Sawayama and Benimaru Itoh
key_artists.why: This credit matters because both artists sit close to Creatures' early 3D/game apparatus. The card is not only an illustration of a Stadium; it is a little tournament-object made by people who also shaped how Pokémon looked and moved in games.

claims.text: The local catalog models the Tōhoku World Challenge Summer participation-prize source group as one row containing Lucky Stadium at source index 171.

Bulbapedia says Lucky Stadium was first awarded to participants of the Japanese World Challenge Summer tournaments held between July and August 2000, with eight variations printed, each one exclusive to a region of Japan.
Bulbapedia lists the Tōhoku print, featuring Diglett, as available at Sendai Wasse, Sendai on August 6, 2000.

PokeBoon identifies Lucky Stadium [Diglett] [Tohoku] as a World Challenge Summer participation prize and gives the Diglett/Tohoku identity, while showing an April 29, 2000 distribution date that this dossier treats as a secondary-source date conflict against Bulbapedia's August 6 Summer event listing.
Bulbapedia's Lucky Stadium gallery credits the Tōhoku region print to Yuichi Sawayama and Benimaru Itoh.
PokeBoon also credits Lucky Stadium [Diglett] [Tohoku] to Benimaru Itoh and Yuichi Sawayama.

Bulbapedia says Yuichi Sawayama worked for Creatures, Inc. as a Pokémon modeler, provided Pokémon TCG illustrations, and has game credits on Hey You, Pikachu!, Pokémon Snap, Pokémon Stadium, Pokémon Stadium 2, Pokémon Channel, Pokémon Colosseum, and Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness.

Bulbapedia describes Benimaru Itoh as a manga artist, designer, and musician who drew for Nintendo franchises, worked at Creatures as 3D modelling director for the Pokémon Stadium games, illustrated Pokémon Newspaper Strip comics, and contributed TCG card artwork.
Bulbapedia says all World Challenge Summer Lucky Stadium prints feature regional landmarks; the Tōhoku print features Godaido Shrine among the islands of Matsushima.

Bulbapedia separates the regional World Challenge Summer prints from the Tropical Mega Battle bilingual print, Neo Destiny English print, Intro Pack Neo print, and Pokemon Center New York print, each of which has different artwork or route.

As judged collector texture, the Tōhoku print matters because Diglett turns the regional Stadium idea inward: not a legendary bird or towering cityscape, but a small ground Pokémon set against shrine-and-island geography.

narrative.human_title: Lucky Stadium [Diglett] [Tōhoku]: the small Pokémon by the islands
narrative.why_it_matters: The Tōhoku print has a quieter magic than the louder regional Lucky Stadiums. Diglett is tiny, almost hidden, and the landmark is Godaido Shrine among Matsushima's islands. That gives the card a grounded kind of charm: a tournament prize that feels local, coastal, and a little secretive, with a small Pokémon peeking through a large regional memory.
not_claiming: resolution of every secondary-source date conflict

special_identification_instructions.trigger: Use when a card, listing, image, or agent claim says Lucky Stadium, Tōhoku, Tohoku, Diglett, World Challenge Summer, Sendai, Godaido Shrine, or Matsushima.
special_identification_instructions.summary: First establish the Tōhoku/Diglett/Summer route, then keep it separate from other regional Lucky Stadium prints and from later or bilingual Lucky Stadium releases.
steps: Check that the card is Lucky Stadium / ラッキースタジアム and that the claimed route is World Challenge Summer participation prize, not Neo Destiny, Intro Pack Neo, Tropical Mega Battle, or Pokemon Center New York.
Confirm the regional identity is Tōhoku / Tohoku and the depicted Pokémon cue is Diglett; do not substitute the other regional mascots such as Lugia, Ho-Oh, Pikachu, Zapdos, Mew, Onix, or Gyarados.
Look for the Tōhoku landmark cue: Godaido Shrine among the islands of Matsushima, and treat generic shrine, island, or coastal language as insufficient unless tied back to this region.

Record Bulbapedia's August 6, 2000 Sendai Wasse, Sendai listing as the current event-route anchor, while preserving PokeBoon's April 29, 2000 date as a visible secondary-source conflict rather than resolving it silently.
Treat source-page identity, artist credit, and release route as catalog legibility only; require seller photos, possession evidence, and card-condition evidence before a transaction gate.
not_claiming: that a matching landmark or mascot alone proves the card is the Tōhoku print

claims.text: The local catalog row identifies source index 171 as Lucky Stadium, a Trainer/Stadium card from the World Challenge Summer participation-prize Tōhoku conference slice, with Diglett as the Pokémon cue.
Bulbapedia identifies the Tōhoku World Challenge Summer Lucky Stadium print as the Diglett variant available at Sendai Wasse, Sendai on August 6, 2000.
PokeBoon identifies the card as Lucky Stadium [Diglett] [Tohoku], unnumbered, and a World Challenge Summer participation prize.
Bulbapedia says the Tōhoku print features Godaido Shrine among the islands of Matsushima.
Bulbapedia and PokeBoon both credit Lucky Stadium [Diglett] [Tōhoku] to Yuichi Sawayama and Benimaru Itoh.

As interpretive art context, the Sawayama/Itoh pairing gives this Diglett Stadium a strong Creatures-era feel: 3D modeling, game-world construction, and TCG card art are touching the same little regional prize.

The Tōhoku print should be separated from the other World Challenge Summer regional prints, the Tropical Mega Battle bilingual print, Neo Destiny, Intro Pack Neo, Pokemon Center New York, and generic Lucky Stadium listings because those carry different route, artwork, or language context.

As judged collector texture, Lucky Stadium [Diglett] [Tōhoku] is interesting because the smallest Pokémon cue in the regional set carries one of the most place-specific scenic cues: shrine, islands, coast, and tournament route.

narrative.human_title: Lucky Stadium [Diglett] [Tōhoku]: a little ground line through Matsushima
narrative.why_it_matters: Diglett makes this Lucky Stadium feel almost intimate. The other regional prints can announce themselves with legendary birds, towers, volcanoes, and city skylines; Tōhoku gives you a small ground Pokémon and the island-shrine landscape of Matsushima. It is still a tournament participation card, but the emotional hook is quieter: the card asks you to notice place, not just power.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: Use when evaluating a specific card image, listing, slab label, or seller claim for Lucky Stadium [Diglett] [Tōhoku].
special_identification_instructions.summary: Identify this card by the combined Tōhoku + Diglett + Godaido Shrine/Matsushima + World Challenge Summer route, not by Lucky Stadium name alone.
steps: Confirm the card name is Lucky Stadium / ラッキースタジアム and that the row is unnumbered promotional, not Neo Destiny 100/105 or another numbered print.
Confirm the variant claim says Tōhoku / Tohoku and shows Diglett; if it shows a different Pokémon, route to the matching regional Lucky Stadium instead.
Check the artwork cue against Godaido Shrine among Matsushima's islands; do not accept a generic regional label without image or source support.

If a source or listing uses April 29, 2000, preserve it as a secondary-source conflict unless supported by a stronger event archive; do not replace Bulbapedia's August 6, 2000 Sendai Wasse anchor without evidence.
Before spending or trade gating, ask for seller-controlled photos and evidence of the actual card; catalog identity is legible support, not physical truth.
